sentences.zh: 布智兒

translations.literal: Buzhier
translations.idiomatic: Buzhier

sentences.zh: 布智兒，蒙古脫脫裏臺氏。

translations.literal: Buzhier, of the Mongol Tottolita clan.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhier belonged to the Mongol Tottolita clan.

sentences.zh: 父紐兒傑，身長八尺，有勇力，善騎射，能造弓矢。

translations.literal: His father Niuerjie was eight chi in height, had courage and strength, was skilled at mounted archery, and could make bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: His father Niuerjie stood eight feet tall, possessed great strength, excelled at riding and shooting, and was adept at crafting bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 嘗道逢太祖前驅騎士別那顏，邀與俱見太祖，視其所挾弓矢甚佳，問誰為造者，對曰：「臣自為之。

translations.literal: Once on the road he met Bieyan, a cavalryman of the Great Khan's advance guard, who invited him to go together to see the Great Khan; [the Khan] saw the bow and arrows he carried were excellent and asked who had made them; he replied, "Your subject made them himself."
translations.idiomatic: Once while traveling he encountered Bieyan of the Khan's vanguard, who invited him to an audience with Genghis Khan. Seeing the fine bow and arrows Niuerjie carried, the Khan asked who had crafted them. Niuerjie answered, "I made them myself, Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」適有野鳧翔於前，射之，獲其二，並以二矢獻而退。

translations.literal: " Just then wild ducks were flying before him; he shot them and obtained two, and presented the two arrows as well and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Just then a flock of wild ducks flew overhead. He shot two of them down and presented both the ducks and the two arrows he had used, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 別那顏隨之，至所居，布智兒出見，別那顏奇之，許以女妻之，父子遂俱事太祖。

translations.literal: Bieyan followed him to his dwelling; Buzhier came out to meet him; Bieyan marveled at him and promised his daughter in marriage to him; father and son then both served the Great Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Bieyan followed him home. When Buzhier came out to greet him, Bieyan was so impressed that he promised his daughter in marriage to the young man. Father and son thereafter both entered the Khan's service.

sentences.zh: 嘗從征討，賜紐兒傑拔都名。

translations.literal: He once followed on campaigns; Niuerjie was granted the name Batu.
translations.idiomatic: Having campaigned with the Khan, Niuerjie was granted the honorific name Batu.

sentences.zh: 從征回回、斡羅思等國，每臨陣，布智兒奮身力戰。

translations.literal: On campaigns against the Muslim lands, Rus, and other states, whenever battle was joined Buzhier threw himself into the fight with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: On campaigns against the Muslim states, Rus, and other realms, Buzhier threw himself into every battle with reckless courage.

sentences.zh: 身中數矢，太祖親視之，令人拔其矢，血流滿體，悶仆幾絕。

translations.literal: He was struck by several arrows; the Great Khan personally looked in on him and ordered men to pull out the arrows; blood flowed over his whole body and he collapsed in a faint, nearly dead.
translations.idiomatic: He was struck by several arrows. The Khan came to see him personally and ordered the arrows removed. Blood streamed over his entire body, and he collapsed unconscious, nearly dead.

sentences.zh: 太祖命取一牛，剖其腹，納布智兒於牛腹，浸熱血中，移時遂甦。

translations.literal: The Great Khan ordered a cow taken, its belly cut open, and Buzhier placed inside the belly and immersed in the hot blood; after a time he revived.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan ordered a cow slaughtered, its belly opened, and Buzhier placed inside to soak in the warm blood. After a time he regained consciousness.

sentences.zh: 紐兒傑卒，憲宗以布智兒為大都行天下諸路也可紥魯忽赤，印造寶鈔。

translations.literal: When Niuerjie died, Emperor Xianzong appointed Buzhier as Yeke Bolqu of all routes under the Dadu circuit, printing precious paper notes.
translations.idiomatic: After Niuerjie's death, Emperor Möngke appointed Buzhier chief overseer of all circuits under the Dadu administration, with responsibility for printing paper currency.

sentences.zh: 賜七寶金帶燕衣十襲，又賜蔚州、定安為食邑。

translations.literal: He was granted a seven-jewel gold belt and ten suits of swallow-tail robes, and furthermore granted Weizhou and Ding'an as fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: He received a gold belt set with seven jewels and ten court robes, and was granted Weizhou and Ding'an as his personal fiefs.

sentences.zh: 布智兒卒，有子四人。

translations.literal: When Buzhier died he had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhier left four sons at his death.

sentences.zh: 長好禮，事世祖，備宿衛。

translations.literal: The eldest, Haoli, served Emperor Shizu and was assigned to the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son, Haoli, entered the service of Kublai Khan as a member of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 會丞相伯顏伐宋，奏好禮督水軍攻襄樊，從渡江入臨安，以功授昭毅大將軍、水軍翼萬戶府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: When the Chancellor Bayan campaigned against Song, [Haoli] memorialized that Haoli should supervise the naval forces attacking Xiangyang and Fancheng; he followed in crossing the Yangtze and entering Lin'an, and for his merit was appointed General of Manifest Valor and Darughachi of the Naval Wing Ten-thousand Households Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Bayan launched the campaign against the Song, Haoli was assigned to command the naval forces assaulting Xiangyang and Fancheng. He crossed the Yangtze with the army and entered Lin'an, and for his service was appointed General of Manifest Valor and military governor of the Naval Wing Ten-thousand Households.

sentences.zh: 別帖木兒，吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Bietiemuer, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Bietiemuer served as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 補兒答思，雲南宣慰使。

translations.literal: Bu'erdasi, Pacification Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Bu'erdasi served as Pacification Commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 不蘭奚，襲父職，為水軍翼萬戶招討使，鎮守江陰，移通州。

translations.literal: Bulanxi inherited his father's post as Naval Wing Ten-thousand Households Pacification Commissioner, garrisoned Jiangyin, and was transferred to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bulanxi inherited his father's position as commander of the Naval Wing Ten-thousand Households, first garrisoning Jiangyin and later transferring to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 子完者不花，遼陽省理問。

translations.literal: His son Wanbuzhehua, Judicial Inquirer of Liaoyang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wanbuzhehua served as Judicial Inquirer of Liaoyang Province.

sentences.zh: ○召烈臺抄兀兒

translations.literal: ○ Zhaolietai Chaowuer
translations.idiomatic: ○ Zhaolietai Chaowuer

sentences.zh: 召烈臺抄兀兒，初事太祖，時有哈剌赤、散只兀、朵魯班、塔塔兒、弘吉剌、亦乞列思等，居堅河之濱忽蘭也兒吉之地，謀奉紥木合為帝，將不利於太祖。

translations.literal: Zhaolietai Chaowuer first served the Great Khan; at that time the Qarachi, Sanjiwu, Doroban, Tatar, Hongjila, Yiqiliesi, and others dwelt at Hulan Yierji on the banks of the Jian River and plotted to install Jamuqa as emperor, intending harm to the Great Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolietai Chaowuer entered the Khan's service early on. At that time the Qarachi, Sanjiwu, Doroban, Tatar, Hongjila, Yiqiliesi, and other tribes living at Hulan Yierji on the banks of the Kerulen River plotted to install Jamuqa as khan, intending to do harm to Genghis Khan.

sentences.zh: 抄兀兒知其謀，馳以告太祖，遂以兵收海剌兒阿帶亦兒渾之地，盡誅紥木合等。

translations.literal: Chaowuer learned of their plot, galloped to inform the Great Khan, and [the Khan] then took troops to seize the lands of Hailar and Yierhun and executed Jamuqa and the rest entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Chaowuer learned of the conspiracy and rode at once to warn the Khan, who then marched his forces to seize the territory of Hailar and Yierhun and put Jamuqa and his allies to death.

sentences.zh: 惟弘吉剌入降。

translations.literal: Only the Hongjila submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Hongjila clan submitted in surrender.

sentences.zh: 太祖賜以答剌罕之名。

translations.literal: The Great Khan granted him the name of Darqan.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan granted him the title of Darqan.

sentences.zh: 闊闊不花

translations.literal: Kuokuobuhua
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuobuhua

sentences.zh: 闊闊不花者，按攤脫脫裏氏，為人魁岸，有膂力，以善射知名。

translations.literal: Kuokuobuhua was of the Atan Tottolita clan; as a man he was tall and imposing, had physical strength, and was renowned for skill in archery.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuobuhua, of the Atan Tottolita clan, was a man of imposing stature and great physical strength, renowned throughout the army for his skill as an archer.

sentences.zh: 歲庚寅，太祖命太師木華黎伐金，分探馬赤為五部，各置將一人，闊闊不花為五部前鋒都元帥，所向莫能支。

translations.literal: In the year gengyin the Great Khan ordered Grand Preceptor Muqali to campaign against Jin, divided the tamma forces into five divisions each with one commander, and Kuokuobuhua was supreme commander of the vanguard of the five divisions; wherever he went none could withstand him.
translations.idiomatic: In the year 1230 the Khan ordered Grand Preceptor Muqali to campaign against the Jin dynasty, dividing the reconnaissance cavalry into five divisions each under its own commander. Kuokuobuhua was appointed supreme commander of the vanguard of all five divisions, and wherever he advanced no enemy could stand against him.

sentences.zh: 然不嗜殺，惟欲以威信懷附，故所至無殘破。

translations.literal: Yet he did not delight in killing; he only wished to win submission through prestige and good faith, so wherever he went there was no devastation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had no taste for slaughter and sought only to win people over through prestige and good faith, so the territories he passed through suffered no devastation.

sentences.zh: 略定濱、棣諸州，俘獲焦林諸處民四百餘，但籍其姓名，遣歸鄉里。

translations.literal: He pacified Bin, Di, and other prefectures; captured more than four hundred people from Jiaolin and other places, but only registered their names and sent them back to their villages.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying the prefectures of Bin and Di, he took more than four hundred civilians from Jiaolin and surrounding areas prisoner, registered their names, and sent them home unharmed.

sentences.zh: 徇益都，守將降，得其財物馬畜，悉以分賜士卒。

translations.literal: He marched on Yidu; the defending commander surrendered; he obtained their goods, horses, and livestock and distributed them all to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When he advanced on Yidu and its defending commander surrendered, he distributed all captured goods, horses, and livestock among his troops.

sentences.zh: 歲壬辰，從太宗渡河，攻汴梁、歸德，分兵渡淮，攻壽州，守將無降意，射書城中諭之，城中人感泣，以彩輿奉金公主開門送款，闊闊不花下令軍中，輒入城虜掠者死，城中帖然。

translations.literal: In the year renchen he followed Emperor Taizong in crossing the river, attacked Bianliang and Guide, divided troops to cross the Huai, and attacked Shouzhou; the defending commander had no intention of surrendering; he shot a letter into the city to instruct them; the people in the city wept with emotion; with a decorated carriage they presented the Jin princess and opened the gates to offer surrender; Kuokuobuhua issued an order in the army that whoever entered the city to plunder and seize would die; the city was entirely at peace.
translations.idiomatic: In 1232 he followed Emperor Ögedei across the Yellow River to attack Bianliang and Guide, then sent detachments across the Huai to assault Shouzhou. When its commander refused to surrender, Kuokuobuhua shot a proclamation into the city. The inhabitants wept at his words, and escorted the Jin princess in a decorated carriage to open the gates in submission. Kuokuobuhua then decreed death for any soldier who entered the city to loot, and Shouzhou remained entirely tranquil.

sentences.zh: 公主，義宗之姑也。

translations.literal: The princess was the paternal aunt of Emperor Yizong.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was a paternal aunt of Emperor Yizong of Jin.

sentences.zh: 歲丙申，太宗命五部將分鎮中原，闊闊不花鎮益都、濟南，按察兒鎮平陽、太原，孛羅鎮真定，肖乃臺鎮大名，怯烈臺鎮東平，括其民匠，得七十二萬戶，以三千戶賜五部將。

translations.literal: In the year bingshen Emperor Taizong ordered the five division commanders to garrison separately in the Central Plains: Kuokuobuhua garrisoned Yidu and Jinan, Anchar garrisoned Pingyang and Taiyuan, Boluo garrisoned Zhending, Xiaonaitai garrisoned Daming, and Qielietai garrisoned Dongping; they registered the civilian craftsmen and obtained 720,000 households, of which three thousand households were granted to the five division commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In 1236 Emperor Ögedei assigned the five division commanders to garrison different regions of north China: Kuokuobuhua at Yidu and Jinan, Anchar at Pingyang and Taiyuan, Boluo at Zhending, Xiaonaitai at Daming, and Qielietai at Dongping. A census of civilians and craftsmen yielded 720,000 registered households, of which three thousand were granted to the five commanders.

sentences.zh: 闊闊不花得分戶六百，立官治其賦，得薦置長吏，歲從官給其所得五戶絲，以疾卒官。

translations.literal: Kuokuobuhua received six hundred allotted households, established officials to administer their taxes, was permitted to recommend and appoint chief officials, and each year received from the government the five-households silk from his revenues; he died in office from illness.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuobuhua received six hundred allotted households, established officials to collect their taxes, and was permitted to recommend local administrators. Each year the government paid him the silk tribute due from his allotment. He died in office of illness.

sentences.zh: 子黃頭，代領探馬赤為元帥，從丞相伯顏取宋，道死。

translations.literal: His son Huangtou succeeded in command of the tamma as marshal, followed Chancellor Bayan in conquering Song, and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huangtou succeeded him as commander of the reconnaissance cavalry and followed Chancellor Bayan in the conquest of the Song, but died en route.

sentences.zh: 子東哥馬襲其職，累遷右都威衛千戶，卒。

translations.literal: His son Donggema inherited his post, was repeatedly promoted to chiliarch of the Right Capital Guard, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Donggema inherited the post and rose through successive promotions to chiliarch of the Right Capital Guard before his death.

sentences.zh: ○拜延八都魯

translations.literal: ○ Baiyan Badoulu
translations.idiomatic: ○ Baiyan Badoulu

sentences.zh: 拜延八都魯，蒙古紥剌臺氏，幼事太祖，賜名八都魯。

translations.literal: Baiyan Badoulu was of the Mongol Zhala clan; in youth he served the Great Khan and was granted the name Badoulu.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyan Badoulu, of the Mongol Zhala clan, entered the Khan's service as a youth and was granted the name Badoulu.

sentences.zh: 歲乙未，太宗命領紥剌軍一千六百人，與塔海甘卜同征關西，有功。

translations.literal: In the year yiwei Emperor Taizong ordered him to lead 1,600 Zhala troops and campaign in Guanxi together with Tahai Ganbu, with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1235 Emperor Ögedei ordered him to lead 1,600 Zhala troops on a campaign in Guanxi alongside Tahai Ganbu, where he distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，憲宗命與阿脫、總帥汪世顯創立利州城。

translations.literal: In guichou Emperor Xianzong ordered him together with Atuo and Commander-in-Chief Wang Shixian to establish the city of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1253 Emperor Möngke ordered him, together with Atuo and Commander-in-Chief Wang Shixian, to found the city of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，領兵紫金山，破宋軍鹿角寨，奪其軍餉器械。

translations.literal: In jiayin he led troops at Zijin Mountain, broke the Song army's Lujiao Stockade, and seized their provisions and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1254 he led troops at Zijin Mountain, stormed the Song army's Lujiao Stockade, and captured their provisions and equipment.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，從都元帥紐鄰城成都，及領兵圍雲頂山，下其城。

translations.literal: In dingsi he followed Supreme Commander Niulin in besieging Chengdu, and also led troops to besiege Yunding Mountain and take its city.
translations.idiomatic: In 1257 he followed Supreme Commander Niulin in the siege of Chengdu and led troops to invest Yunding Mountain, which fell to his assault.

sentences.zh: 帝親征，元帥紐鄰既進兵，涉馬湖江，留拜延八都魯鎮成都，降屬縣諸城，得其民，悉撫安之，賜黃金五十兩、衣九襲。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned in person, after Supreme Commander Niulin had advanced his troops and crossed the Mahu River, he left Baiyan Badoulu to garrison Chengdu; the subordinate counties and cities all surrendered; he obtained their people and entirely pacified and settled them; he was granted fifty taels of gold and nine suits of robes.
translations.idiomatic: During the Emperor's personal campaign, after Supreme Commander Niulin advanced his forces across the Mahu River, he left Baiyan Badoulu to garrison Chengdu. The surrounding counties and towns all submitted, and he pacified the local population. He was rewarded with fifty taels of gold and nine suits of robes.

sentences.zh: 諸王哈丹、朵歡、脫脫等征大理還，命拜延八都魯領兵迎之。

translations.literal: When the princes Hadan, Duohuan, Toto, and others returned from campaigning in Dali, [the Emperor] ordered Baiyan Badoulu to lead troops to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: When Princes Hadan, Duohuan, Toto, and others returned from the campaign against Dali, the Emperor ordered Baiyan Badoulu to lead troops to meet them.

sentences.zh: 道過新津寨，與宋潘都統遇，戰敗之，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Passing Xinjin Stockade on the way, he encountered Song Commander Pan, defeated him in battle, and killed and captured a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Xinjin Stockade en route, he encountered Song Commander Pan, routed his forces, and killed or captured a great number of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，元帥紐鄰上其功，授蒙古奧魯官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong, Supreme Commander Niulin reported his merit and he was appointed Mongol Auru official.
translations.idiomatic: In 1261 Supreme Commander Niulin submitted a report of his achievements, and he was appointed overseer of the Mongol civilian population.

sentences.zh: 子外貌臺，孫兀渾察。

translations.literal: His son Waiguotai, grandson Wuhuncha.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Waiguotai; his grandson was Wuhuncha.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，拜延八都魯告老，兀渾察代其軍，從行省也速答兒征諸國有功。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan, Baiyan Badoulu retired; Wuhuncha succeeded his army and followed the Branch Secretariat Yasudar in campaigning in various states with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1269 Baiyan Badoulu retired from service. Wuhuncha took command of his forces and campaigned under Branch Secretariat Yasudar in various regions, distinguishing himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 十六年，從大軍征斡端，又有功，賞銀五十兩。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he followed the great army in campaigning against Woduan and again had merit; he was rewarded with fifty taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In 1279 he joined the main army's campaign against Woduan and again distinguished himself, receiving a reward of fifty taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，諸王術伯命兀渾察往乞失哈裏之地為遊擊軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Prince Shubo ordered Wuhuncha to go to the land of Qishihali as a mobile strike force.
translations.idiomatic: In 1284 Prince Shubo assigned Wuhuncha to lead a mobile strike force in the region of Qishihali.

sentences.zh: 時敵軍二千餘，兀渾察以勇士五十人與戰，擒其將也班胡火者以獻。

translations.literal: At that time the enemy numbered more than two thousand; Wuhuncha with fifty brave warriors engaged them in battle and captured their commander Yebanhuhuozhe and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: Facing an enemy force of more than two thousand, Wuhuncha attacked with only fifty picked warriors, captured their commander Yebanhuhuozhe, and presented him as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 王壯之，以其功聞，賞銀六百兩、鈔四千五百貫，授蒙古軍萬戶，賜三珠虎符。

translations.literal: The prince admired this and reported his merit; he was rewarded with six hundred taels of silver and 4,500 strings of paper notes, appointed Ten-thousand Households of the Mongol army, and granted a three-pearl tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was so impressed that he reported the feat to court. Wuhuncha received six hundred taels of silver and 4,500 strings of paper currency, was appointed commander of a Mongol ten-thousand household, and was granted a three-pearl tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 三十年，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1293 he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 次子襲授曲先塔林左副元帥，尋卒。

translations.literal: The second son inherited and was appointed Left Deputy Marshal of Quxiantalin, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: His second son inherited the post as Left Deputy Marshal of Quxiantalin but died soon after.

sentences.zh: 弟塔海忽都襲，升鎮國上將軍都元帥，改授四川蒙古副都萬戶。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tahai Hudu inherited, was promoted to General for Pacifying the State and Supreme Commander, and was reassigned as Deputy Commander of Ten-thousand Households of the Mongol forces in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Tahai Hudu inherited the command, rose to the rank of General for Pacifying the State and Supreme Commander, and was reassigned as deputy commander of the Mongol ten-thousand households in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，以疾退。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi he retired due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1322 he retired due to illness.

sentences.zh: 子孛羅帖木兒襲。

translations.literal: His son Boluotiemuer inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Boluotiemuer inherited the post.

sentences.zh: ○阿術魯

translations.literal: ○ Ashilu
translations.idiomatic: ○ Ashilu

sentences.zh: 阿術魯，蒙古氏。

translations.literal: Ashilu, of the Mongol clan.
translations.idiomatic: Ashilu was a Mongol.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，命同飲班朱尼河之水，扈駕親征有功，命領兵收附遼東女直，還，賞金甲、珠衣、寶帶，他物稱是。

translations.literal: In the time of the Great Khan he was ordered to drink the waters of the Baljuna River together [with the Khan], escorted the imperial carriage on personal campaigns with merit, was ordered to lead troops to receive and attach the Jurchen of eastern Liaodong; on return he was rewarded with a gold armor, pearl garments, and a precious belt, and other things in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: During Genghis Khan's reign he was among those who drank the waters of the Baljuna River as a pledge of loyalty, accompanied the Khan on personal campaigns with distinction, and was then ordered to lead troops in subduing the Jurchen of eastern Liaodong. On his return he received a suit of golden armor, pearl-embroidered robes, a jeweled belt, and comparable gifts besides.

sentences.zh: 復命總兵征西夏，與敵兵大戰於合剌合察兒之地。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to command troops in campaigning against Western Xia and fought a great battle with the enemy at Helahecha'er.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to command the campaign against Western Xia and fought a major battle with the enemy at Helahecha'er.

sentences.zh: 西夏勢蹙，其主懼，乞降，執之以獻，太宗殺之，賜以所籍貲產。

translations.literal: Western Xia's situation was desperate; its ruler was afraid and begged to surrender; [Ashilu] seized him and presented him; Emperor Taizong killed him and granted [Ashilu] the confiscated property.
translations.idiomatic: With Western Xia's position collapsing, its ruler sued for peace in fear. Ashilu seized him and presented him to Ögedei Khan, who had the ruler executed and granted Ashilu the confiscated property.

sentences.zh: 繼領兵收附信安，下金二十餘城。

translations.literal: He subsequently led troops to receive and attach Xin'an and captured more than twenty Jin cities.
translations.idiomatic: He then led troops to subdue Xin'an and captured more than twenty Jin cities.

sentences.zh: 其後告老，諸王塔察兒命其子不花代領其軍。

translations.literal: Afterward he retired; Prince Tachar ordered his son Buhua to succeed in command of his army.
translations.idiomatic: He later retired from active service, and Prince Tachar appointed his son Buhua to succeed him in command of his forces.

sentences.zh: ○紹古兒

translations.literal: ○ Shaoguer
translations.idiomatic: ○ Shaoguer

sentences.zh: 紹古兒，麥裏吉臺氏。

translations.literal: Shaoguer, of the Mailijita clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoguer belonged to the Mailijita clan.

sentences.zh: 事太祖，命同飲班朱尼河之水，扈從親征。

translations.literal: He served the Great Khan, was ordered to drink the waters of the Baljuna River together [with the Khan], and escorted [him] on personal campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He served Genghis Khan, drank the waters of the Baljuna River as a pledge of loyalty, and accompanied the Khan on his personal campaigns.

sentences.zh: 已而從破信安，略地河西，賜金虎符，授洺磁等路都達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Subsequently he followed in capturing Xin'an and pacifying the Hexi region; he was granted a gold tiger tally and appointed Chief Darughachi of the Mingci and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He then took part in the capture of Xin'an and the pacification of the Hexi region, for which he received a gold tiger tally and was appointed chief military governor of the Mingci and surrounding circuits.

sentences.zh: 領軍出征，復從伐金，破河南。

translations.literal: Leading troops on campaign, he again followed in attacking Jin and broke Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Leading troops on campaign, he again joined the assault on the Jin dynasty and broke through Henan.

sentences.zh: 太宗命領濟南、大名、信安等處軍馬，復從國王答石出征。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong ordered him to command the military forces of Jinan, Daming, Xin'an, and other places, and he again followed Prince Dashi on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ögedei placed him in command of the forces at Jinan, Daming, Xin'an, and other posts, and he again campaigned under Prince Dashi.

sentences.zh: 歲辛亥，卒。

translations.literal: In the year xinhai he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the year 1251.

sentences.zh: 子拜都襲。

translations.literal: His son Baidu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baidu inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 拜都卒，子忽都虎襲，移睢州。

translations.literal: When Baidu died, his son Huduhu inherited and was transferred to Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Baidu's death, his son Huduhu inherited the command and was transferred to Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 從世祖渡江，攻鄂，還鎮恩州。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Shizu in crossing the Yangtze, attacked Ezhou, and returned to garrison Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangtze with Kublai Khan in the assault on Ezhou, then returned to garrison Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，從征李亶有功，尋命修立邳州城，領兵鎮兩淮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong he followed the campaign against Li Tan with merit; soon he was ordered to repair and build the city of Pizhou and lead troops to garrison the Two Huai [region].
translations.idiomatic: In 1262 he distinguished himself in the campaign against Li Tan, then was ordered to rebuild the walls of Pizhou and take command of the garrison along the Two Huai region.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從丞相伯顏渡江，有戰功。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he followed Chancellor Bayan in crossing the Yangtze and had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1274 he crossed the Yangtze with Chancellor Bayan and distinguished himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 又從參政董文炳沿海出征，還，鎮嘉興，行安撫事。

translations.literal: He again followed Vice Councillor Dong Wenbing on a coastal campaign; on return he garrisoned Jiaxing and performed pacification duties.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Vice Councillor Dong Wenbing's coastal expedition, and on returning was stationed at Jiaxing with authority over local pacification.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加昭勇大將軍，職如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to General of Manifest Courage, his duties remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 1275 he was promoted to General of Manifest Courage while retaining his existing duties.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授嘉興路總管府達魯花赤，尋升鎮國上將軍、黃州路宣慰使，尋罷黃州宣慰司，復舊任。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Darughachi of the Jiaxing Circuit General Administration Office; soon he was promoted to General for Pacifying the State and Pacification Commissioner of Huangzhou Circuit; soon the Huangzhou Pacification Commission was abolished and he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277 he was appointed military governor of Jiaxing, then promoted to General for Pacifying the State and Pacification Commissioner of Huangzhou. When the Huangzhou Pacification Commission was abolished soon after, he resumed his former post at Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 十六年，改授浙西道宣慰使，加招討使，仍鎮國上將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was reassigned as Pacification Commissioner of the Zhexi Circuit, with the added title of Pacification Commissioner, still holding the rank of General for Pacifying the State.
translations.idiomatic: In 1279 he was reassigned as Pacification Commissioner of the Zhexi Circuit with the additional title of Pacification Commissioner, retaining the rank of General for Pacifying the State.

sentences.zh: 奉詔征占城，以其國降表、貢物入見，帝嘉之，厚加賞賚。

translations.literal: By imperial decree he campaigned against Champa; he presented himself with that state's letter of surrender and tribute goods; the Emperor praised him and richly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial decree he campaigned against Champa and presented himself at court bearing the kingdom's letter of surrender and tribute gifts. The Emperor was greatly pleased and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，從征交趾。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he followed the campaign against Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1287 he joined the campaign against Annam.

sentences.zh: 明年還師，授邳州萬戶府萬戶。

translations.literal: The following year the army returned; he was appointed Ten-thousand Households of the Pizhou Ten-thousand Households Office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after the army's return, he was appointed commander of the Pizhou Ten-thousand Households.

sentences.zh: 三十年，沒於軍。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1293 he died on campaign.

sentences.zh: ○阿剌瓦而思

translations.literal: ○ Alawaersi
translations.idiomatic: ○ Alawaersi

sentences.zh: 阿剌瓦而思，回鶻八瓦耳氏，仕其國為千夫長。

translations.literal: Alawaersi was of the Uighur Bawar clan and served his state as chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: Alawaersi, of the Uighur Bawar clan, had served his kingdom as a chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 太祖征西域，駐蹕八瓦耳之地，阿剌瓦而思率其部曲來降。

translations.literal: When the Great Khan campaigned in the Western Regions and halted at Bawar, Alawaersi led his tribal forces to come and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Genghis Khan campaigned in the Western Regions and encamped at Bawar, Alawaersi led his tribal forces to submit.

sentences.zh: 從帝親征，既破瀚海軍，又攻輪臺、高昌、于闐、尋斯幹等，靡戰不克，沒於軍。

translations.literal: He followed the Emperor on personal campaigns; after breaking the Hanhai army he also attacked Luntai, Gaochang, Yutian, Xunsigan, and others; there was no battle he did not conquer; he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the Khan on personal campaigns, defeating the Hanhai forces and then conquering Luntai, Gaochang, Yutian, Xunsigan, and other cities without a single failure, until he fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 子阿剌瓦丁，從世祖北征有功，至元二十九年卒，壽一百二歲。

translations.literal: His son Alawading followed Emperor Shizu on the northern campaign with merit; in the twenty-ninth year of Zhiyuan he died, aged one hundred and two.
translations.idiomatic: His son Alawading distinguished himself in Kublai Khan's northern campaign and died in 1292 at the age of one hundred and two.

sentences.zh: 子贍思丁，有子五人：長烏馬兒，陳州達魯花赤；

translations.literal: His son Shansiding had five sons: the eldest Wumaer, Darughachi of Chenzhou;
translations.idiomatic: His son Shansiding had five sons: the eldest, Wumaer, served as military governor of Chenzhou;

sentences.zh: 次不別，隆鎮衛都指揮使；

translations.literal: the second Bubie, Commander of the Longzhen Guard;
translations.idiomatic: the second, Bubie, as Commander of the Longzhen Guard;

sentences.zh: 次忻都，監察御史；

translations.literal: the third Xindu, Investigating Censor;
translations.idiomatic: the third, Xindu, as Investigating Censor;

sentences.zh: 次阿合馬，拱衛直司都指揮使；

translations.literal: the fourth Ahema, Commander of the Archery Guard Direct Office;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth, Ahema, as Commander of the Archery Guard;

sentences.zh: 次阿散不別，驍勇善騎射，歷事成宗、武宗、仁宗，數被寵遇，計前後所賜楮幣余四十萬緡，他物稱是，積官榮祿大夫，三珠虎符。

translations.literal: the fifth Asan Bubie, valiant and skilled at mounted archery, served through the reigns of Emperor Chengzong, Wuzong, and Renzong, was repeatedly favored; counting the paper notes granted before and after, more than 400,000 strings, and other things in proportion; he accumulated the office of Grand Master for Glorious Blessing and a three-pearl tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: the youngest, Asan Bubie, a man of great courage skilled at riding and shooting, served through the reigns of Emperors Chengzong, Wuzong, and Renzong and was repeatedly honored at court. The paper currency he received over his career totaled more than 400,000 strings, with comparable gifts besides, and he rose to the rank of Grand Master for Glorious Blessing with a three-pearl tiger tally.

sentences.zh: ○抄兒

translations.literal: ○ Chao'er
translations.idiomatic: ○ Chao'er

sentences.zh: 抄兒，別速氏。

translations.literal: Chao'er, of the Biesu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Chao'er belonged to the Biesu clan.

sentences.zh: 世居汴梁陽武縣，從太祖收附諸國有功。

translations.literal: His family had long dwelt in Yangwu County of Bianliang; he followed the Great Khan in receiving and attaching the various states with merit.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long resided in Yangwu County near Bianliang. He followed Genghis Khan in the subjugation of various states and distinguished himself in the process.

sentences.zh: 又從征金，沒於陣。

translations.literal: He again followed in campaigning against Jin and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the campaign against the Jin and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 子抄海，從征河南、山東，復沒於陣。

translations.literal: His son Chaohai followed campaigns in Henan and Shandong and again died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chaohai campaigned in Henan and Shandong and likewise fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 子別帖，將其父軍，從攻鄂州，以功賞銀帛衣甲等，繼從太子忽哥赤西征大理國，復沒於陣。

translations.literal: His son Bietie commanded his father's army, followed in attacking Ezhou, and for his merit was rewarded with silver, silks, armor, and the like; he subsequently followed Crown Prince Huguoshi on the western campaign against the Dali kingdom and again died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bietie took command of his father's forces, joined the assault on Ezhou, and was rewarded with silver, silks, armor, and the like for his service. He then followed Crown Prince Huguoshi on the western expedition against Dali and fell in battle as well.

sentences.zh: 子阿必察，至元五年授武略將軍、蒙古千戶，賜金符，從圍襄樊，復渡江，奪陽羅堡岸口，以功賞白金，進宣武將軍、蒙古軍總管，管領左右手兩萬戶軍。

translations.literal: His son Abicha, in the fifth year of Zhiyuan was appointed General of Martial Strategy and Mongol chiliarch, granted a gold tally; he followed in besieging Xiangyang and Fancheng, again crossed the Yangtze, seized the shore at Yangluo Fort, and for his merit was rewarded with white gold; he was promoted to General of Manifest Martiality and Commander of the Mongol army, commanding the left and right two ten-thousand household forces.
translations.idiomatic: His son Abicha was appointed General of Martial Strategy and commander of a Mongol chiliarch in 1268, granted a gold tally. He joined the siege of Xiangyang and Fancheng, crossed the Yangtze again, and seized the shore at Yangluo Fort. Rewarded with white gold for his service, he was promoted to General of Manifest Martiality and overall commander of the Mongol forces, with authority over both left and right ten-thousand household armies.

sentences.zh: 既下廣德，從平章阿裏海牙征海外國，率死士鼓戰船進，奪岸口，擒勇士趙安等，以功賞銀帛。

translations.literal: After Guangde fell he followed Pacification Commissioner Alihaiya in campaigning against overseas states, led dare-to-die troops beating war boats forward, seized the shore, and captured the warrior Zhao An and others; for his merit he was rewarded with silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Guangde he joined Pacification Commissioner Alihaiya's expedition against overseas states, leading picked troops in a frontal assault on the war fleet, seizing the shore and capturing the warrior Zhao An and others. He was rewarded with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 十六年，命管領蒙古侍衛軍，以疾卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was ordered to command the Mongol palace guard army and died of illness in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1279 he was placed in command of the Mongol palace guard and died of illness on campaign.

sentences.zh: ○也蒲甘卜

translations.literal: ○ Yepuganbu
translations.idiomatic: ○ Yepuganbu

sentences.zh: 也蒲甘卜，唐兀氏。

translations.literal: Yepuganbu was of the Tangut clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yepuganbu was a Tangut.

sentences.zh: 歲辛巳，率眾歸太祖，隸蒙古軍籍。

translations.literal: In the year xinsi he led his people to submit to the Great Khan and was enrolled in the Mongol military registers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1221 he led his followers to submit to Genghis Khan and was enrolled in the Mongol military registers.

sentences.zh: 奉旨同所管河西人，從木華黎出征，以疾卒。

translations.literal: By imperial decree he together with the Hexi people under his command followed Muqali on campaign and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial decree he led the Hexi people under his command on campaign with Muqali and died of illness en route.

sentences.zh: 子昂吉兒襲領其軍，征諸國有功。

translations.literal: His son Angu'er inherited command of his army and campaigned in various states with merit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Angu'er inherited his command and distinguished himself in campaigns across several regions.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，授金符千戶，從征蘄、黃、安慶等處。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed gold-tally chiliarch and followed campaigns in Qi, Huang, Anqing, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In 1269 he was appointed chiliarch with a gold tally and campaigned in Qi, Huang, Anqing, and other regions.

sentences.zh: 九年，易虎符，升信陽萬戶，從平章阿術南征，又有功，歷淮西道宣慰使、參知政事、都元帥、廬州蒙古漢軍萬戶府達魯花赤、行省左丞相、尚書左丞，積官龍虎衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he exchanged his tiger tally and was promoted to Xinyang Ten-thousand Households; he followed Pacification Commissioner Ashu on the southern campaign and again had merit; he served successively as Pacification Commissioner of the Huaixi Circuit, Vice Councillor, Supreme Commander, Darughachi of the Luzhou Mongol and Han Ten-thousand Households Office, Left Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat, and Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat, accumulating the office of General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1272 he received a new tiger tally and was promoted to commander of Xinyang Ten-thousand Households. He followed Pacification Commissioner Ashu on the southern campaign with further distinction, rising through Pacification Commissioner of Huaixi, Vice Councillor, Supreme Commander, military governor of the Luzhou Mongol and Han Ten-thousand Households, Left Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat, and Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat, eventually attaining the rank of General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，攜其子昂阿禿入見。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he brought his son Ang'atu to an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In 1284 he presented his son Ang'atu at court.

sentences.zh: 世祖命昂阿禿充速古兒赤。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu ordered Ang'atu to serve as sugurji.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai Khan appointed Ang'atu to the imperial guard corps known as sugurji.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，隨駕征乃顏有功，奉旨代其父職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he followed the imperial carriage in campaigning against Nayan with merit and was ordered by decree to succeed his father's post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1287 he accompanied the Emperor on the campaign against Nayan with distinction and was ordered by decree to succeed his father.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授廬州蒙古漢軍萬戶府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Darughachi of the Luzhou Mongol and Han Ten-thousand Households Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1289 he was appointed military governor of the Luzhou Mongol and Han Ten-thousand Households.

sentences.zh: 大德六年，領兵討宋隆濟等，以功受上賞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dade he led troops to suppress Song Longji and others and received a superior reward for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1302 he led troops against Song Longji and others and received a superior reward for his service.

sentences.zh: 還鎮廬州，以私財築室一百二十餘間，以居軍士之貧者，省臺以其事聞，特命升其秩，以金束帶賜之。

translations.literal: Returning to garrison Luzhou, he built more than 120 rooms at his private expense to house poor soldiers; the provincial and central offices reported this matter, and he was specially ordered promoted in rank and granted a gold-banded belt.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to garrison Luzhou, he built more than 120 rooms at his own expense to shelter impoverished soldiers. When the provincial and central offices reported this to court, he was specially promoted and granted a gold-banded belt.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiding he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1327.

sentences.zh: 昂阿禿之弟暗普，由速古兒赤授金符、唐兀禿魯花千戶，後改授海北海南道廉訪使。

translations.literal: Ang'atu's younger brother Anpu, from sugurji was appointed gold tally and Tangut Tuluhua chiliarch, and later was reassigned as Surveillance Commissioner of the Haibei and Hainan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Ang'atu's younger brother Anpu rose from the sugurji guard to appointment as chiliarch with a gold tally over the Tangut Tuluhua, and was later reassigned as Surveillance Commissioner of the Haibei and Hainan Circuit.

sentences.zh: ○趙阿哥潘

translations.literal: ○ Zhao'agepan
translations.idiomatic: ○ Zhao'agepan

sentences.zh: 趙阿哥潘，土播思烏思臧掇族氏。

translations.literal: Zhao'agepan was of the Tubosi Wusizangduo clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao'agepan belonged to the Tubosi Wusizangduo clan.

sentences.zh: 始附宋，賜姓趙氏。

translations.literal: He first submitted to Song and was granted the surname Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He initially submitted to the Song and was granted the surname Zhao.

sentences.zh: 世居臨洮。

translations.literal: His family had long dwelt in Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long resided in Lintao.

sentences.zh: 祖巴命，富甲諸羌。

translations.literal: His grandfather Baming was wealthier than all the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Baming was the wealthiest man among the Qiang tribes.

sentences.zh: 父阿哥昌，貌甚偉，有力兼人，金貞祐中，以軍功至熙河節度使。

translations.literal: His father Agechang was very imposing in appearance and had strength surpassing others; in the Zhenyou era of Jin, through military merit he rose to Military Commissioner of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: His father Agechang was a man of imposing stature with strength surpassing ordinary men. During the Jin dynasty's Zhenyou era he rose through military merit to Military Commissioner of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 金亡，保蓮花山，以其眾來歸。

translations.literal: When Jin perished he held Lotus Mountain and came with his forces to submit.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Jin dynasty he held Lotus Mountain and came with his followers to submit.

sentences.zh: 皇子闊端之鎮西土也，承制以阿哥昌為疊州安撫使。

translations.literal: When Prince Kuoduan was stationed in the western lands, by provisional order Agechang was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Diezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Kuoduan governed the western territories, he appointed Agechang Pacification Commissioner of Diezhou by provisional authority.

sentences.zh: 時兵興，城無居人，至則招逃亡，立城壘，課耕桑以安輯之，年八十，卒於官。

translations.literal: At that time warfare was raging and the city had no inhabitants; on arrival he summoned back fugitives, built walls and ramparts, and imposed farming and sericulture to settle and pacify them; at age eighty he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: War was raging and the city stood empty when he arrived. He summoned back those who had fled, rebuilt the walls, and promoted farming and sericulture to restore order. He died in office at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 阿哥潘事親以孝聞，從伐蜀，與宋都統制曹友聞屢戰，勝負略相當，以破大安功最，授同知臨洮府事。

translations.literal: Zhao'agepan was known for filial service to his parents; following the campaign against Shu he fought repeatedly with Song Commander Cao Youwen, victories and defeats being roughly equal; for breaking Da'an his merit was greatest and he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Lintao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned for filial devotion to his parents, Zhao'agepan joined the campaign against Shu and fought repeatedly against Song Commander Cao Youwen with roughly equal success. His greatest achievement was the capture of Da'an, for which he was appointed Vice Commissioner of Lintao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 斬朝天關，乘嘉陵江至閬州，獲蜀船三百艘。

translations.literal: He cut through Chaotian Pass, reached Langzhou along the Jialing River, and obtained three hundred Shu boats.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Chaotian Pass, advanced along the Jialing River to Langzhou, and seized three hundred Shu boats.

sentences.zh: 攻利州，生得其劉太尉，戰敗宋師於川。

translations.literal: Attacking Lizhou, he captured the Liu Grand Marshal alive; he defeated Song forces in the river region.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Lizhou he took Grand Marshal Liu alive and routed Song forces in the river region.

sentences.zh: 宋制置使劉雄飛進攻青居山，阿哥潘擊之，宵潰，四川大震。

translations.literal: Song Commissioner Liu Xiongfei advanced to attack Qingju Mountain; Zhao'agepan struck him and at night he fled in rout; all Sichuan was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Commissioner Liu Xiongfei advanced on Qingju Mountain, Zhao'agepan attacked him and drove his forces into a rout by night, throwing all of Sichuan into alarm.

sentences.zh: 進逼成都，略嘉定，平峨眉太平寨，擒其將陳侍郎、田太尉，余眾悉降。

translations.literal: He pressed on to Chengdu, pacified Jiading, and took Taiping Stockade at Emei, capturing their generals Vice Minister Chen and Grand Marshal Tian; the rest all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed toward Chengdu, pacified Jiading, and captured Taiping Stockade at Emei along with Song generals Vice Minister Chen and Grand Marshal Tian. The remaining defenders all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 大小五十餘戰，皆先陷陣，皇子賜以金甲、銀器。

translations.literal: In more than fifty battles large and small he always charged at the front of the formation; the prince rewarded him with golden armor and silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In more than fifty engagements, large and small, he always led the charge. The prince rewarded him with golden armor and silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 歲壬子，世祖以皇弟南征大理，道出臨洮，見而奇之，命攝元帥，城益昌。

translations.literal: In the year renzi Emperor Shizu as imperial younger brother campaigned south against Dali; passing through Lintao he saw him and marveled, ordering him to act as marshal and build up Yichang city.
translations.idiomatic: In 1252 Kublai Khan, then campaigning south against Dali as imperial younger brother, passed through Lintao, was struck by Zhao'agepan's abilities, and appointed him acting marshal to build up the city of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 時宋兵屯兩川，堡柵相望，矢石交擊，歷五年而城始完。

translations.literal: At that time Song troops were stationed in the two Sichuan circuits, stockades and forts facing one another, arrows and stones exchanged in attack; after five years the city was finally completed.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces held both Sichuan circuits with stockades and forts facing one another across a constant exchange of arrows and stones. Five years passed before the city walls were finally completed.

sentences.zh: 憲宗出蜀，以阿哥潘為選鋒，攻西安，下之，賜金符，授臨洮府元帥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong marched out of Shu he made Zhao'agepan vanguard; he attacked Xi'an and took it; he was granted a gold tally and appointed Marshal of Lintao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Möngke marched out of Shu, Zhao'agepan served as vanguard, attacked Xi'an, and captured it. He received a gold tally and was appointed marshal of Lintao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝駐釣魚山，合州守將王堅夜來斫營，阿哥潘率壯士逆戰，手殺數十百人，堅遂引去。

translations.literal: When the Emperor encamped at Diaoyu Mountain, Hezhou defending commander Wang Jian came by night to cut the camp; Zhao'agepan led stalwart warriors to meet the attack and with his own hand killed several tens of men; Jian then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: While the Emperor encamped at Diaoyu Mountain, Hezhou's defending commander Wang Jian launched a night assault on the camp. Zhao'agepan led picked warriors to meet the attack and personally killed dozens of men, forcing Wang Jian to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 明日陛見，帝喜曰：「有臣如此，朕復何憂！

translations.literal: The next day at audience the Emperor said with pleasure, "With a subject such as this, what have I to worry about!
translations.idiomatic: At audience the next day the Emperor said with pleasure, "With a subject such as this, what have I to fear!

sentences.zh: 」賜黃金五十兩，名曰拔都。

translations.literal: " He granted fifty taels of gold and bestowed the name Batu.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted fifty taels of gold and bestowed the name Batu.

sentences.zh: 中統建元，詔還鎮臨洮。

translations.literal: When Zhongtong was established as the reign title, an edict ordered him back to garrison Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhongtong reign was proclaimed, an edict recalled him to garrison Lintao.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，發私廩以賑貧乏。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he opened his private granaries to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year he opened his private granaries to relieve the destitute.

sentences.zh: 給民農種粟二千餘石、蕪菁子百石，人賴不饑。

translations.literal: He gave the people more than two thousand piculs of seed grain and a hundred piculs of turnip seed; the people relied on this and did not starve.
translations.idiomatic: He distributed more than two thousand piculs of seed grain and a hundred piculs of turnip seed to the people, who were thereby spared starvation.

sentences.zh: 郡當孔道，傳置旁午，有司敝於供給。

translations.literal: The prefecture lay on a major thoroughfare and relay stations were constantly busy; officials were worn out by provisioning.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture lay on a major thoroughfare with relay traffic unceasing, and officials were exhausted by the burden of provisioning.

sentences.zh: 阿哥潘以私馬百匹充驛騎，羊千口代民輸。

translations.literal: Zhao'agepan supplied a hundred private horses for relay service and a thousand sheep in place of the people's levies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao'agepan contributed a hundred of his own horses for relay service and a thousand sheep in lieu of the people's transport levies.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而嘉之，詔京兆行省酬其直。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of this he praised it and ordered the Jingzhao Branch Secretariat to reimburse their value.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised this act and ordered the Jingzhao Branch Secretariat to reimburse him.

sentences.zh: 阿哥潘曰：「我豈以私惠而邀公賞耶！

translations.literal: Zhao'agepan said, "How could I use private kindness to seek public reward!
translations.idiomatic: Zhao'agepan replied, "How could I use private generosity to seek public reward!

sentences.zh: 」卒不受。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused to accept payment.

sentences.zh: 以軍事赴青居山，道為宋兵所邀，遂死於敵。

translations.literal: Going on military business to Qingju Mountain, on the road he was intercepted by Song troops and thus died at the hands of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: While traveling on military business to Qingju Mountain, he was intercepted by Song troops and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 阿哥潘好畜良馬，常千蹄，歲擇其上驥五駟貢於朝，子孫遵之不替。

translations.literal: Zhao'agepan delighted in raising fine horses, constantly a thousand hooves; each year he selected the finest five teams of four to present as tribute at court, and descendants observed this without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao'agepan delighted in raising fine horses, keeping as many as a thousand at a time. Each year he selected the finest teams of four to present as tribute at court, a practice his descendants maintained without interruption.

sentences.zh: 先是，勛臣子孫為祖父請謚者，帝每靳之，至是敕大臣以美謚謚之，謚曰桓勇。

translations.literal: Previously, when meritorious subjects' descendants requested posthumous titles for their grandfathers, the Emperor always withheld them; now he ordered the great ministers to bestow a fine posthumous title on him, posthumous name Huan Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Emperor had routinely withheld posthumous titles sought by descendants of meritorious subjects. Now he ordered his ministers to grant Zhao'agepan the posthumous title Huan Yong.

sentences.zh: 官卓斯結性靖退，辭官閑處二十餘年。

translations.literal: Guan Zhuosijie by nature was retiring and resigned office to live in seclusion for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhuosijie, a man of retiring disposition, resigned office and lived in seclusion for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 仁宗聞其名，召不起。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong heard his name and summoned him, but he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong heard of him and summoned him, but he refused to come.

sentences.zh: 子德壽，雲南左丞。

translations.literal: His son Deshou, Left Vice Minister of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Deshou served as Left Vice Minister of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: ○純只海

translations.literal: ○ Chunzhihai
translations.idiomatic: ○ Chunzhihai

sentences.zh: 純只海，散術臺氏。

translations.literal: Chunzhihai was of the Sanshutai clan.
translations.idiomatic: Chunzhihai belonged to the Sanshutai clan.

sentences.zh: 弱冠宿衛太祖帳下，從征西域諸國有功。

translations.literal: In his youth he served in the Great Khan's guard tent and followed campaigns in the Western Regions with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served in Genghis Khan's guard and distinguished himself in campaigns across the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 歲癸巳，太宗命佩金虎符，充益都行省軍民達魯花赤，從大帥太出破徐州，擒金帥國用安。

translations.literal: In the year guisi Emperor Taizong ordered him to wear the gold tiger tally and appointed him Chief Darughachi of the military and civilians of the Yidu Branch Secretariat; he followed Grand Marshal Tachu in breaking Xuzhou and captured the Jin commander Guo Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In 1233 Emperor Ögedei ordered him to wear the gold tiger tally as chief military governor of the Yidu Branch Secretariat. He followed Grand Marshal Tachu in the capture of Xuzhou and took the Jin commander Guo Yong'an prisoner.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以益都為皇太子分土，遷京兆行省都達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In dingyou Yidu became the crown prince's fief; he was transferred to Chief Darughachi of the Jingzhao Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1237, when Yidu became the crown prince's fief, he was transferred to chief military governor of the Jingzhao Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至懷，值大疫，士卒困憊，有旨以本部兵就鎮懷孟。

translations.literal: Arriving at Huai, he encountered a great epidemic; soldiers were exhausted and weary; an order directed his command to garrison at Huai and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Huai he encountered a great epidemic that left his soldiers exhausted. An order directed his forces to garrison Huai and Meng.

sentences.zh: 未幾，代察罕總軍河南，尋復懷孟。

translations.literal: Before long he replaced Chahan in overall command of the Henan army, and soon returned to Huai and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he replaced Chahan as overall commander of the Henan army, then soon returned to Huai and Meng.

sentences.zh: 己亥，同僚王榮潛畜異志，欲殺純只海，伏甲縶之，斷其兩足跟，以帛緘純只海口，置佛祠中。

translations.literal: In jihai his colleague Wang Rong secretly harbored rebellious intent and wished to kill Chunzhihai; he set armed men to seize him, cut both his heel tendons, bound Chunzhihai's mouth with cloth, and placed him in a Buddhist shrine.
translations.idiomatic: In 1239 his colleague Wang Rong secretly plotted rebellion and attempted to kill Chunzhihai. Wang set armed men to seize him, severed both his Achilles tendons, bound his mouth with cloth, and left him in a Buddhist shrine.

sentences.zh: 純只海妻喜禮伯倫聞之，率其眾攻榮家，奪出之。

translations.literal: When Chunzhihai's wife Xilibolun heard of this she led her followers to attack Rong's house and rescued him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chunzhihai's wife Xilibolun learned of this, she led her followers in an assault on Wang Rong's house and rescued her husband.

sentences.zh: 純只海裹瘡從二子馳旁郡，請兵討榮，殺之。

translations.literal: Chunzhihai wrapped his wounds and with his two sons galloped to a neighboring prefecture to request troops to punish Rong and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wrapping his wounds, Chunzhihai rode with his two sons to a neighboring prefecture to raise troops, then returned to kill Wang Rong.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣使以榮妻孥貲產賜純只海家，且盡驅懷民萬餘口郭外，將戮之。

translations.literal: The court sent envoys to grant Wang Rong's wife, children, and property to Chunzhihai's family, and moreover drove more than ten thousand Huai residents outside the walls, intending to slaughter them.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys granting Wang Rong's wife, children, and property to Chunzhihai's family and ordered more than ten thousand residents of Huai driven outside the walls for execution.

sentences.zh: 純只海力爭曰：「為惡者止榮一人耳，其民何罪。

translations.literal: Chunzhihai argued forcefully, saying, "The one who did evil was only Rong alone; what crime have the people committed?
translations.idiomatic: Chunzhihai argued forcefully: "Only Wang Rong committed evil. What crime have the common people committed?

sentences.zh: 若果盡誅，徒守空城何為？

translations.literal: If they are indeed all put to death, of what use is merely holding an empty city?
translations.idiomatic: If they are all put to death, of what use is holding an empty city?

sentences.zh: 茍朝廷罪使者以不殺，吾請以身當之。

translations.literal: If the court would punish the envoy for not killing them, I ask to answer for it with my own person.
translations.idiomatic: If the court would punish the envoy for failing to carry out the slaughter, I ask to answer for it with my own life.

sentences.zh: 」使者還奏，帝是其言，民賴不死。

translations.literal: " The envoy returned to report; the Emperor approved his words and the people relied on this and did not die.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy returned and reported to the Emperor, who approved his argument. The people were spared.

sentences.zh: 純只海給榮妻孥券，放為民，遂以其宅為官廨，秋毫無所取。

translations.literal: Chunzhihai issued certificates to Wang Rong's wife and children and released them as commoners; he then made their residence the government office and took not the slightest thing.
translations.idiomatic: Chunzhihai issued certificates freeing Wang Rong's wife and children as commoners, converted their residence into the government office, and took nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 郡人德之。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the prefecture revered him for this.

sentences.zh: 既入覲，太宗以純只海先朝舊臣，功績昭著，賜第一區於和林，尋以疾卒。

translations.literal: After entering for audience, Emperor Taizong because Chunzhihai was an old minister of the previous reign with illustrious achievements granted him a first-ranked residence at Karakorum; soon he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After he presented himself at court, Emperor Ögedei, recognizing Chunzhihai as a veteran minister of the previous reign with illustrious service, granted him a first-ranked residence at Karakorum. He soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 敕葬山陵之側。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him buried beside the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him buried beside the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 皇慶初，贈推忠宣力功臣、金紫光祿大夫、上柱國、溫國公，謚忠襄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangqing he was posthumously granted the title of Merit Subject for Loyal Promotion of Power, Grand Master of the Golden Purple and Bright Light, Pillar of the State, Duke of Wen, posthumous name Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huangqing era he was posthumously granted the title Merit Subject for Loyal Promotion of Power, Grand Master of the Golden Purple and Bright Light, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Wen, with the posthumous name Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 仍敕詞臣劉敏中制文樹碑於懷，以旌其功云。

translations.literal: He was further ordered that the literary minister Liu Minzhong compose a text and erect a stele at Huai to proclaim his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: The literary minister Liu Minzhong was further ordered to compose an inscription and erect a stele at Huai to proclaim his achievements.

sentences.zh: 子昂阿剌嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ang'ala succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ang'ala succeeded him.

sentences.zh: ○苫徹拔都兒

translations.literal: ○ Shanchebadouer
translations.idiomatic: ○ Shanchebadouer

sentences.zh: 苫徹拔都兒，欽察人。

translations.literal: Shanchebadouer was a Kipchak.
translations.idiomatic: Shanchebadouer was a Kipchak.

sentences.zh: 初事太宗，掌牧馬。

translations.literal: He first served Emperor Taizong and managed horse herds.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Emperor Ögedei as overseer of the horse herds.

sentences.zh: 從攻鳳翔，戰潼關，皆有功。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Fengxiang and fought at Tong Pass, all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the attacks on Fengxiang and the battle at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 後從大將速不臺攻汴京，金人列木柵於河南，苫徹拔都兒率死士往拔之，賜良馬十匹。

translations.literal: Later he followed the great general Subutai in attacking Bianjing; the Jin erected wooden palisades south of the river; Shanchebadouer led dare-to-die troops to go pull them up and was granted ten fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed the great general Subutai in the assault on Bianjing. When the Jin erected wooden palisades south of the river, Shanchebadouer led picked troops to tear them down and was rewarded with ten fine horses.

sentences.zh: 師還，金將高都尉率眾邀於中路，苫徹拔都兒迎擊，斬其首以歸，賜白金五十兩、幣四匹。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Jin Vice Commander Gao led troops to intercept on the middle road; Shanchebadouer met the attack, cut off his head, and returned; he was granted fifty taels of white gold and four bolts of silks.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, Jin Vice Commander Gao intercepted them on the march. Shanchebadouer met the attack, severed Gao's head, and was rewarded with fifty taels of white gold and four bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 從攻蔡州，前鋒答答兒與金將戰，金將捽其須，苫徹拔都兒進斫金將，乃得脫。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Caizhou, the vanguard Dadar fought with a Jin commander; the Jin commander seized his beard; Shanchebadouer advanced and cut down the Jin commander, and [Dadar] was thus able to escape.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Caizhou, the vanguard Dadar was seized by the beard in combat with a Jin commander. Shanchebadouer advanced and cut the Jin commander down, allowing Dadar to escape.

sentences.zh: 蔡州破，金守將佩虎符立城上，苫徹拔都兒以鐵椎擊殺之，取虎符以獻。

translations.literal: When Caizhou fell a Jin defending commander wearing a tiger tally stood atop the wall; Shanchebadouer struck and killed him with an iron mace and took the tiger tally to present.
translations.idiomatic: When Caizhou fell, a Jin defending commander wearing a tiger tally stood atop the wall. Shanchebadouer struck him down with an iron mace, seized the tally, and presented it.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其能，命從皇子攻棗陽。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his ability and ordered him to follow the prince in attacking Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his prowess and ordered him to follow the prince in the attack on Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 繼從宗王口溫不花攻光州，一日五戰，光州下。

translations.literal: He subsequently followed Prince Kouwenbuhua in attacking Guangzhou; in one day there were five battles and Guangzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: He subsequently followed Prince Kouwenbuhua in the attack on Guangzhou, fighting five engagements in a single day until the city fell.

sentences.zh: 賜黃金五十兩、白金酒器一事、馬三十匹。

translations.literal: He was granted fifty taels of gold, one set of white-gold wine vessels, and thirty horses.
translations.idiomatic: He received fifty taels of gold, a set of white-gold wine vessels, and thirty horses.

sentences.zh: 百戶愛不怯赤自以臨陣不勇，乞苫徹拔都兒自代，遂升百戶。

translations.literal: Chiliarch Aibuqiechi, considering himself not brave in battle, begged that Shanchebadouer replace him, and [Shanchebadouer] was then promoted to chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: Chiliarch Aibuqiechi, judging himself insufficiently brave in battle, asked that Shanchebadouer replace him, and Shanchebadouer was promoted to chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 從攻滁州，與宋兵大戰，至暮，宋兵敗走西山，苫徹拔都兒與千戶忽孫追殺之。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Chuzhou he fought a great battle with Song troops; by evening Song troops were defeated and fled to the western hills; Shanchebadouer with chiliarch Husun pursued and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Chuzhou he fought a major engagement with Song forces. By evening the Song army fled west into the hills, and Shanchebadouer with chiliarch Husun pursued and slaughtered them.

sentences.zh: 歲己未，世祖伐宋，募能先絕江者，苫徹拔都兒首應命，率眾逼南岸。

translations.literal: In the year jiwei Emperor Shizu campaigned against Song and recruited those able to cross the river first; Shanchebadouer was the first to answer the call and led his forces to press the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1259 Kublai Khan campaigned against the Song and sought men able to cross the Yangtze first. Shanchebadouer was the first to volunteer and led his forces to the south bank.

sentences.zh: 詔苫徹拔都兒與脫歡領兵百人。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Shanchebadouer together with Tuohan to command a hundred troops.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Shanchebadouer and Tuohan to command a hundred troops.

sentences.zh: 同宋使諭鄂州使降。

translations.literal: Together with Song envoys they instructed Ezhou to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Song envoys they went to demand the surrender of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 抵城下，鄂守將殺使者以軍來襲，苫徹拔都兒與之遇，奮擊大破之。

translations.literal: Arriving below the city, the Ezhou defending commander killed the envoys and came with an army to attack; Shanchebadouer encountered them and struck fiercely, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the city, Ezhou's commander killed the envoys and led troops out to attack. Shanchebadouer met them head-on and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 復賜黃金五十兩。

translations.literal: He was again granted fifty taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He was again rewarded with fifty taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，授蔡州蒙古漢軍萬戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong he was appointed Ten-thousand Households of the Caizhou Mongol and Han army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1262 he was appointed commander of the Caizhou Mongol and Han ten-thousand households.

sentences.zh: 冬，宋人犯西平，苫徹拔都兒逐北逾淮，獲其生口甚眾。

translations.literal: In winter Song troops invaded Xiping; Shanchebadouer pursued them north beyond the Huai and captured a great many prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when Song forces invaded Xiping, Shanchebadouer pursued them north beyond the Huai and took many prisoners.

sentences.zh: 至元二年秋，由安慶入廬州，聞宋兵至，亟設伏於竹林，擊殺之。

translations.literal: In the second year autumn of Zhiyuan, entering from Anqing into Luzhou, hearing Song troops had arrived he quickly set an ambush in a bamboo grove and struck and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 1265, advancing from Anqing into Luzhou, he heard that Song troops had arrived, quickly set an ambush in a bamboo grove, and annihilated them.

sentences.zh: 四年秋九月，元帥阿術軍襄陽安陽灘。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, autumn, ninth month, Marshal Ashu stationed his army at Anyangtan of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of 1267, Marshal Ashu stationed his army at Anyangtan near Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 宋兵據渡口，苫徹拔都兒擊破其眾。

translations.literal: Song troops held the crossing; Shanchebadouer broke their forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Song forces held the river crossing, Shanchebadouer broke through their lines.

sentences.zh: 五年，從阿術圍襄陽，擊奪宋將夏貴米舟。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Ashu in besieging Xiangyang and in attack seized Song commander Xia Gui's grain boats.
translations.idiomatic: In 1268 he joined Ashu's siege of Xiangyang and in the fighting seized the grain boats of Song commander Xia Gui.

sentences.zh: 阿術入漢江，以其有戰功，俾與紥剌兒引軍南略，獲八十人。

translations.literal: Ashu entered the Han River; because of his battle merit he was ordered together with Zhala'er to lead troops south in raiding and obtained eighty men.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashu entered the Han River, Shanchebadouer was ordered, for his battle merit, to join Zhala'er in a southern raid and captured eighty men.

sentences.zh: 十年八月，略地淮東。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, eighth month, he raided Huaidong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of 1273 he conducted raids in Huaidong.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遣招鄂州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was sent to summon Ezhou to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In 1274 he was dispatched to summon Ezhou to surrender.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遣招滁州，誅王安撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was sent to summon Chuzhou to surrender and executed the pacification commissioner Wang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1275 he was sent to summon Chuzhou to surrender and executed Pacification Commissioner Wang.

sentences.zh: 改武略將軍、管軍千戶。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as General of Martial Strategy and chiliarch commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as General of Martial Strategy and commander of a chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 五月，伏兵大江北岸，擊宋軍，敗走之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he set an ambush on the north bank of the great river, struck Song troops, and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he ambushed Song forces on the north bank of the Yangtze and drove them into flight.

sentences.zh: 十三年，復略地淮東，獲其總管二人以獻。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he again raided Huaidong and captured two of their commanders-in-chief to present.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276 he again raided Huaidong and presented two captured Song commanders-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 遷滁州總管府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Darughachi of the Chuzhou General Administration Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military governor of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋都統姜才率軍取糧高郵，苫徹拔都兒從史萬戶奪其馬及糧橐二萬，淮東平，入朝。

translations.literal: Song Commander Jiang Cai led troops to take grain at Gaoyou; Shanchebadouer with Ten-thousand Households Shi seized their horses and twenty thousand grain bags; when Huaidong was pacified he entered court.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Commander Jiang Cai led troops to seize grain at Gaoyou, Shanchebadouer joined Ten-thousand Households Shi in seizing their horses and twenty thousand grain sacks. After Huaidong was pacified he presented himself at court.

sentences.zh: 十四年，從討叛人只裏瓦歹於懷剌合都，改宣武將軍、滁州路總管府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed in suppressing the rebel Zhiliwadai at Huailahedu and was reassigned as General of Manifest Martiality and Darughachi of the Chuzhou Circuit General Administration Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277 he joined the suppression of the rebel Zhiliwadai at Huailahedu and was reassigned as General of Manifest Martiality and military governor of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十七年，率其子脫歡、孫麻兀入見。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he led his son Tuohan and grandson Mawu to an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In 1280 he presented his son Tuohan and grandson Mawu at court.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「臣老矣，幸主上憐之。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying, "Your subject is old; may the sovereign pity him.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "I am old, Your Majesty; I beg your compassion.

sentences.zh: 」帝命以脫歡為宣武將軍、管軍總管，佩金符；

translations.literal: " The Emperor ordered Tuohan appointed General of Manifest Martiality and Commander of Troops, wearing a gold tally;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor appointed Tuohan General of Manifest Martiality and overall troop commander with a gold tally;

sentences.zh: 麻兀為滁州路總管府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Mawu as Darughachi of the Chuzhou Circuit General Administration Office.
translations.idiomatic: and Mawu as military governor of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 其後脫歡以征倭功授明威將軍、滁州萬戶府達魯花赤，升昭勇大將軍、征行軍萬戶府達魯花赤，佩三珠虎符。

translations.literal: Subsequently Tuohan for merit in campaigning against Japan was appointed General of Bright Martiality and Darughachi of the Chuzhou Ten-thousand Households Office, promoted to General of Manifest Courage and Darughachi of the Campaigning Ten-thousand Households Office, wearing a three-pearl tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: Tuohan later distinguished himself in the campaign against Japan and was appointed General of Bright Martiality and military governor of Chuzhou Ten-thousand Households, then promoted to General of Manifest Courage and military governor of the Campaigning Ten-thousand Households with a three-pearl tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 又以征爪哇功升昭毅大將軍，鎮守無為滁州萬戶府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Again for merit in campaigning against Java he was promoted to General of Manifest Valor and garrisoned as Darughachi of the Wuwei Chuzhou Ten-thousand Households Office.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in the Java campaign he was further promoted to General of Manifest Valor and appointed military governor of the Wuwei Chuzhou Ten-thousand Households.

sentences.zh: 次子鎖住，襲其職。

translations.literal: The second son Suozhu inherited his post.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Suozhu inherited the post.

sentences.zh: ○怯怯裏

translations.literal: ○ Qieqieli
translations.idiomatic: ○ Qieqieli

sentences.zh: 怯怯裏，斡耳那氏。

translations.literal: Qieqieli was of the Orna clan.
translations.idiomatic: Qieqieli belonged to the Orna clan.

sentences.zh: 太宗七年南伐，以千戶從闊端攻安豐、壽州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taizong's southern campaign he as chiliarch followed Kuoduan in attacking Anfeng and Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Ögedei's seventh-year southern campaign he served as chiliarch under Kuoduan in the attacks on Anfeng and Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 又從諸王塔察兒率蒙古軍二千攻荊山，破之，賜馬二匹。

translations.literal: He again followed Prince Tachar leading two thousand Mongol troops to attack Jingshan, broke it, and was granted two horses.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Prince Tachar with two thousand Mongol troops in the capture of Jingshan and was rewarded with two horses.

sentences.zh: 與萬戶納<角┦>以兵守沂、郯，略漣海，又從元帥懷都攻襄陽。

translations.literal: Together with Ten-thousand Households Narji he held Yin and Tan with troops, raided Lianhai, and again followed Marshal Huaidu in attacking Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Ten-thousand Households Narji he garrisoned Yin and Tan, raided Lianhai, and followed Marshal Huaidu in the attack on Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子相兀速襲父職，率本部兵從丞相阿術攻襄樊，又從塔出築正陽堡。

translations.literal: His son Xiangwusu inherited his father's post, led his command's troops following Chancellor Ashu in attacking Xiangyang and Fancheng, and again followed Tachu in building Zhengyang Fort.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiangwusu inherited his command, led his troops with Chancellor Ashu against Xiangyang and Fancheng, and joined Tachu in building Zhengyang Fort.

sentences.zh: 瀘軍乘艦來窺壁壘，相兀速率征騎逆之，夾淮水而軍，射死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Lu troops came in warships to spy on the walls; Xiangwusu led campaign cavalry to meet them, encamped on both sides of the Huai, and shot dead a great many.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu troops approached in warships to reconnoiter the fortifications, Xiangwusu led cavalry to meet them, drew up on both banks of the Huai, and killed a great many with arrow fire.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，賜金符，授武略將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan he was granted a gold tally and appointed General of Martial Strategy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1274 he received a gold tally and was appointed General of Martial Strategy.

sentences.zh: 明年，從御史大夫博羅罕平漣海。

translations.literal: The following year he followed Censor-in-Chief Boluohan in pacifying Lianhai.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he joined Censor-in-Chief Boluohan in pacifying Lianhai.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，從丞相伯顏渡淮，率兵一千騎攻淮安南門，破之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn he followed Chancellor Bayan in crossing the Huai, led a thousand cavalry to attack Huai'an's south gate, and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he crossed the Huai with Chancellor Bayan, led a thousand horsemen against Huai'an's south gate, and broke through.

sentences.zh: 又從元帥博羅罕築灣頭堡。

translations.literal: He again followed Marshal Boluohan in building Wantou Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Marshal Boluohan in building Wantou Fort.

sentences.zh: 萬戶納兒<角┦>臥疾，令相兀速權領蒙古、女直、漢人三萬戶。

translations.literal: Ten-thousand Households Narji lay ill and ordered Xiangwusu to act in command of the Mongol, Jurchen, and Han three ten-thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Ten-thousand Households Narji fell ill, he placed Xiangwusu in temporary command of the Mongol, Jurchen, and Han three ten-thousand households.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，宋揚州都統姜才引兵來侵，相兀速率本部兵逆戰有功。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer Song Yangzhou Commander Jiang Cai led troops to invade; Xiangwusu led his command's troops to meet the attack with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, when Song Yangzhou Commander Jiang Cai invaded, Xiangwusu led his troops to repel the attack with distinction.

sentences.zh: 又從丞相阿術襲制置使李庭芝及姜才於泰州，皆殺之。

translations.literal: He again followed Chancellor Ashu in a surprise attack on Commissioner Li Tingzhi and Jiang Cai at Taizhou; both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Chancellor Ashu in a surprise attack on Commissioner Li Tingzhi and Jiang Cai at Taizhou, killing both.

sentences.zh: 十四年，加宣武將軍、管軍總管。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to General of Manifest Martiality and Commander of Troops.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277 he was promoted to General of Manifest Martiality and overall troop commander.

sentences.zh: 十八年，為蒙古侍衛親軍總管。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he became Commander of the Mongol Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1281 he became commander of the Mongol Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，改千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was reassigned as chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: In 1286 he was reassigned as chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 三十年，升蒙古侍衛親軍副指揮使司事，易金虎符，加顯武將軍。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was promoted to Deputy Commander of the Mongol Palace Guard, exchanged his gold tiger tally, and was promoted to General of Manifest Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: In 1293 he was promoted to deputy commander of the Mongol Palace Guard, received a new gold tiger tally, and was promoted to General of Manifest Martiality.

sentences.zh: ○塔不已兒

translations.literal: ○ Tabuyier
translations.idiomatic: ○ Tabuyier

sentences.zh: 塔不已兒，束呂糺氏。

translations.literal: Tabuyier was of the Shulüjiu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Tabuyier belonged to the Shulüjiu clan.

sentences.zh: 太宗時以招討使將兵出征，破信安、河南，以功授金虎符、征行萬戶。

translations.literal: In Taizong's time as pacification commissioner he led troops on campaign, broke Xin'an and Henan, and for his merit was granted a gold tiger tally and Campaigning Ten-thousand Households.
